title: He wasn’t supposed to feel anything.
paragraphs: He wasn’t supposed to feel anything.

Not here.
Not now.
Not for this Man.

A Roman soldier doesn’t tremble.
A trained executioner doesn’t question orders.
And yet… something about this crucifixion refused to stay ordinary.
Because this wasn’t just another death.

The sky had already turned strange.
Dark… heavy… like creation itself was holding its breath.

The crowd? Still loud.
Mocking. Spitting. Laughing.
But the Man on the cross… didn’t.

For them.
For you.
For the one holding the spear.
His name, according to early Christian tradition, was Longinus.

A soldier of Rome.
A man of war.
A professional at ending life.
And in that moment, he was given a final task:

Steel in hand.
Eyes fixed.
Heart… still hardened.

The spear rises—
and thrusts into the side of Jesus.
Something no battlefield had ever prepared him for.
“Immediately blood and water came out.” — John 19:34

Some scholars interpret this as a physical sign of death—
the separation of fluids, a pierced heart, a body truly lifeless.
But others—through the centuries—saw something deeper.
A mystery unfolding in real time.
It was the Gospel in liquid form.

Blood — for forgiveness.
Water — for cleansing.
And here’s where the story grips the soul.
Ancient Christian tradition says that when that blood and water touched Longinus…

The man who pierced Jesus…
being the first to be touched by what came out of Him.

The wound he caused—
becomes the source of his healing.

Because this is where religion breaks…
and grace explodes.
For the one who inflicted the wound.

And even if you set aside the physical miracle—
Scripture gives us something just as powerful.
A Roman centurion stood there… watching it all unfold.

The darkness.
The earthquake.
The way Jesus died.
“Truly, this was the Son of God.” — Mark 15:39
A man trained to obey Caesar…
Here’s the truth we don’t like to admit:
We are not just the crowd watching.
We are not just the disciples who ran.
We are the ones who drove the nails.

Our sin.
Our pride.
Our hidden compromises.

Every lie.
Every secret.
Every moment we chose ourselves over God.
It all led to that cross.
is the same Jesus who pours out mercy.

The blood that was shed because of you…
is the blood that can save you.
You think you’ve gone too far?
You think your hands are too dirty?
You think your eyes are too blind?
This is not a story about a soldier.
Because every one of us stands at that cross.

A spear.
A sin.
A secret.

Willing to be pierced…
so you can be made whole.

Willing to bleed…
so you can be forgiven.

Willing to die…
so you can finally live.
The cross is not just where Jesus died.
It’s where your blindness can end.

Maybe today…
you don’t need more information.

The Son of God.
The Lamb who was slain.
The Savior who stayed.
But because grace found you in the moment you least deserved it.
What will you do with the One you’ve pierced?

Ignore Him?
Mock Him?
Walk away?

Or fall to your knees…
and finally see?

Not cleaned up.
Not perfect.
Just honest.
Let the blood speak for you.
Because if grace can reach a Roman soldier with a spear…
